intro.text: An eccentric young woman in Kilahito, one of Akane's friends, who works out Yumi's dramascope when they first meet.
An eccentric nightmare painter in Kilahito, fascinated by hion viewer programs and the inventor of dramascopes.

items.text: Before starting work, Izzy invented dramascopes, a kind of fortune-telling that draws on hion viewer programs alongside more traditional methods. She defended them stubbornly against her friends' doubts, hoping they would make her rich and famous.

At upper school Izzy became friends with Akane, Tojin, Masaka and Nikaro, and shared their belief that Nikaro would make the Dreamwatch and take them on as companions. Finding out he had lied left her deeply distrustful of him. After graduating she became a painter, usually partnering Masaka.
Izzy met Yumi when Akane brought her to the Noodle Pupil, and after shaking her hand she shared Yumi's dramascope.

Izzy joined the friends who coaxed Yumi out to dinner, where she teased Tojin to put his shirt back on for Yumi's sake. When talk turned to Nikaro she changed the subject to their world's spaceship, due to launch soon.

When Yumi was caught hunting the stable nightmare, Izzy was quickest to leave work and keenest that Yumi grasp Nikaro's record of lying, pointing out that a stable nightmare would already have attacked the city.
Izzy was taken aback when Tojin agreed to help Nikaro. During the battle she froze in the middle of an attack, and Nikaro pushed her clear and saved her with a painting of a bird.

appearance.text: About twenty, Izzy is long-limbed with bleached yellow hair. She wears trousers and sweatshirts, sometimes in white to contrast with Masaka's black.

personality.text: Izzy is whimsical, often leaving her friends unsure whether she is serious, and can change the subject suddenly and forcefully. She follows current events closely, is bisexual, and says she would happily date an alien.
The surprise final episode of Seasons of Regret affected her deeply, inspiring her to become a critic of viewer programs and to write a book about their benefits for mental health.
